comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological quality (C9-C18, C102-C104). Both recognize comprehensive tissue preparation protocols, quantitative measurements, and sample sizes as well-supported. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer reviewers explicitly praise 'morphometric and quantitative assays' and accept methods without criticism.

Strong agreement on single-ending observation (C48-C52). Both recognize this as a significant original contribution. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat that functional uniformity inference needs validation; peer reviewers explicitly state 'This in fact is a significant original contribution' and call it 'best support for validity of classification method.'

Both address functional predictions about receptive fields (C60-C66). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes predictions require physiological validation; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN and recommend reducing speculation, noting these are 'inferences about function' that would benefit from physiological or molecular validation.

Partial overlap on genetic system (C1-C5, C99-C101, C125). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for genetic approach and functional normality; peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly praising 'inducible-intersectional genetic strategy' and acknowledging limitations are 'discussed frankly' and 'not an impediment to publication.'

Disagreement on Brn3a hemizygosity concern (C6-C8). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on prior literature justifying functional normality; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'this does not rule out a subtle phenotype' and recommend better acknowledgment of compensatory autoregulation.

Agreement on sampling limitations (C19-C23). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for appropriate acknowledgment of biases; peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, stating 'non-randomness is fully understood by the authors' and limitations are 'discussed frankly.'

Agreement on limitation acknowledgment (C22-C23, C124, C126). Both recognize authors appropriately discuss sampling biases and incomplete coverage. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate these acknowledgments as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on functional correlations (C53-C59). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting inferences lack direct validation but use appropriate qualifying language; peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN but more critically, stating 'Whether the morphological classification system used here really corresponds well to function remains to be seen.'

Agreement on directional sensitivity speculation (C37, C67-C72). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, calling these 'interesting hypotheses requiring physiological testing'; peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN and recommend 'avoid diluting the information with speculation that may or may not be correct.'

Agreement on coverage factor calculations (C75-C79). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting calculations involve extrapolations from incomplete data; peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, recommending focus on clear conclusions rather than speculation.

Agreement on mechanistic speculation (C80-C85). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, calling these 'reasonable hypotheses but remain speculative'; peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN and recommend 'avoid diluting the information with speculation that may or may not be correct.'

Agreement on orientation mechanism (C86-C89). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to reliance on unpublished data; peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, grouping with other speculative mechanistic discussions that should be reduced.

Strong agreement on methodological contribution (C90-C98, C123). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for technical advantages and feasibility demonstration; peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly recognizing 'general implications for many scientists' in the genetic labeling method.

Agreement on classification methodology (C24, C127-C128). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of formal clustering as minor limitation; peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, praising 'morphometric and quantitative assays for categorizing' the results.
Agreement on reproducibility (C105-C106). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for technical reliability demonstration; peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED as part of overall methodological quality recognition.

Disagreement on small arbor interpretation (C29-C31). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about technical limitations; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, suggesting P21 timepoint may not represent mature state and arbors might still be refining.

Agreement on quantitative analysis (C107-C111, C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for parametric comparisons demonstrating arbor type distinctions; peer reviewers implicitly support by recognizing 'quality of the results' and morphometric categorization.

Agreement on depth stratification (C117-C122). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for clear demonstration of stratification patterns; peer reviewers implicitly support through overall recognition of morphometric quality.

Agreement on main finding (C24). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for six arbor type classification based on 719 arbors; peer reviewers implicitly support by stating work 'should be published' and recognizing quality of morphometric categorization.

Agreement on morphological measurements (C32-C33). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for detailed quantitative characterization; peer reviewers implicitly support through overall recognition of result quality.
Agreement on BE arbor characterization (C34). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for specific morphological measurements; peer reviewers implicitly support through overall acceptance of morphometric results.
Agreement on LA-FACE characterization (C35-C37, C71). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for comprehensive quantitative data; peer reviewers implicitly support through overall recognition of result quality.
Agreement on relative abundance (C38). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on large sample size; peer reviewers implicitly support through overall acceptance of quantitative findings.
